validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: The destination facility is strongly, independently real. Al Najibiya power station (محطة كهرباء النجيبية) is a ~500 MW gas/dual-fuel plant in the Al-Najibiya district of Basra city (west bank of the Shatt al-Arab), commissioned Jan 2016, owned by Iraq's Ministry of Electricity, 4x GE 9E gas turbines (power-technology.com profile; INA/ninanews Key=913132 on unit-5 maintenance). The pipeline itself is an OPC (Oil Pipelines Company / شركة خطوط الانابيب النفطية) dry-gas feeder rehabilitation. HOWEVER both citations the sheet uses trace to ONE origin: (a) opc.oil.gov.iq/?article=184 and (b) OPC's own Facebook post (facebook.com/PipelinesIQ) — that is a single institutional source, NOT two independent sources per the 2+ rule. Neither is currently content-verifiable: the OPC site now serves a bot-challenge/secure-gateway redirect (url_verifier gets 200 but the article body tokens النجيبية/الغاز are absent), and the Facebook URL 200s to a login/generic wall (token النجيبية absent). I could NOT find any independent third-party media (Iraqi press, INA, al-Mirbad, alkhaleej, attaqa, powernews) that names this specific Najibiya feeder line — searches surfaced only ANALOGOUS OPC dry-gas feeder projects (Najaf & Kirkuk cement plants, Kirkuk/Qayyarah power-station gas lines) and a separate 40 km/42-inch Khor Al-Zubair→Shatt al-Arab dry-gas trunk to Basra power stations (powernews.cc p=238204 — that is P7435, NOT this line). So the feeder is PLAUSIBLE and consistent with a documented OPC program of supplying Basra power stations with dry gas, but its independent corroboration is effectively zero. CLASSIFICATION: correctly gas (dry gas / الغاز الجاف), correctly NOT one of the GulfPub Iraq crude/NGL lines (none of them serve Najibiya PS). Mild caveat: at 4.5 km / 12 in this is a short dedicated power-station feeder/lateral rather than a trunk — GEM convention files dedicated power-plant gas supply lines as transmission, so 'transmission' is defensible but borderline. DUPLICATE: no other Najibiya row in the 36-line Iraq gas operating roster; not a relabel of any sibling. P7435 (Khor Al-Zubair–Shatt Al Arab, 40 km/42) is the likely upstream trunk that feeds this area, a distinct asset, not a duplicate. ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'Oil Pipelines Co' and Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' are consistent (OPC is a Ministry-of-Oil company and the Facebook page is literally OPC); province Basra and endpoint 'Al Najibiya power station' are correct. SPEC: length 4.5 km, diameter 12 in — single-origin OPC, unverifiable at present, so LOW confidence, not overturned (no conflicting figure found). Capacity blank and left blank (no sourced value).

routes.start_name: Dry-gas supply tap on the Basra dry-gas distribution network (unnamed node, ~4.5 km from the plant; part of the South Gas Company / Khor Al-Zubair-fed trunk serving Basra power stations)
routes.end_name: Al Najibiya power station, Al-Najibiya district, Basra city (west bank of the Shatt al-Arab)
routes.corridor_desc: Short (~4.5 km) 12-inch dry-gas lateral inside Basra city, terminating at the Al Najibiya power station in the Al-Najibiya neighborhood on the west bank of the Shatt al-Arab, just south of central Basra. The upstream end is a tap on the dry-gas network that OPC/South Gas Company is extending to Basra power stations (fed from the Khor Al-Zubair gas complex ~30 km south, via the separate 40 km/42-in Khor Al-Zubair→Shatt al-Arab trunk, P7435). The exact source node and the pipe's routing are NOT published; only the plant end is locatable. The end coordinate is a district-centroid approximation for the named Al-Najibiya neighborhood, NOT a surveyed pipeline terminus — treat as loose. Given 4.5 km, the entire corridor lies within ~5 km of 30.49N/47.81E inside urban/peri-urban Basra.
routes.researcher_notes: End endpoint (Al Najibiya PS) established from the power-technology plant profile (Basra, ~500 MW gas/dual-fuel, GE 9E) plus INA/ninanews maintenance coverage — the facility is unambiguous and lies in the named Al-Najibiya district of Basra. End lat/lon (30.49, 47.81) is a defensible district-level approximation of that named neighborhood, NOT a fabricated precise terminus; flagged approximate. Start node coordinates left NULL — the specific dry-gas tap feeding this 4.5 km lateral is not published anywhere I could source; I decline to invent a point. Corridor/supply context (Khor Al-Zubair-fed dry-gas program to Basra power stations) from powernews.cc p=238204, which documents the parallel 40 km/42-in trunk (P7435) but does NOT name the Najibiya feeder. NO coordinates were fabricated.

summary: Al Najibiya PS gas feeder: endpoint (Basra Najibiya power station) independently confirmed, but the 4.5 km/12-in pipe rests on a single OPC origin (both refs = OPC, currently un-content-verifiable) with zero independent third-party confirmation — confirmed (caveat), concern_type=spec, low tier; route endpoint located to district level (~30.49N,47.81E), start node unresolved.
